extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and Intellectual Property Office (IPO) examiners preparing or evaluating sequence listings under the WIPO ST.26 standard
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and representing nucleotide and amino acid sequence listings in patent applications compliant with WIPO ST.26, including which sequences must/must not be included and how to annotate variants, modifications, and nonstandard symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences required by ST.26 paragraph 6
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.26 paragraph 6 (with certain restrictions) requires inclusion of a sequence disclosed in a patent application by enumeration of its residues where the sequence contains ten or more specifically defined nucleotides or four or more specifically defined amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sequence meets these numeric thresholds it must be included in the sequence listing; evaluate whether residues are 'specifically defined' per ST.26 paragraph 3(h) and whether the sequence is disclosed by 'enumeration of its residues' (paragraph 3(bbis)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on short sequences (paragraph 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.26 paragraph 7 prohibits inclusion of any sequences having fewer than ten specifically defined nucleotides or four specifically defined amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include sequences below the thresholds as separate sequences in the sequence listing. If the disclosure defines alternatives that would create specifically-defined sequences exceeding thresholds, include those alternatives (see examples and recommended additional sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'enumeration of its residues' (paragraph 3(bbis))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Enumeration of its residues' is disclosure of a sequence by listing, in order, each residue of the sequence, wherein (i) the residue is represented by a name, abbreviation, symbol, or structure; or (ii) multiple residues are represented by a shorthand formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequences should be disclosed using conventional symbols (nucleotide symbols in Annex I Section 1 Table 1 and amino acid symbols in Annex I Section 3 Table 3). Symbols other than those tables are 'nonconventional' and require consultation of the disclosure to interpret meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of nonconventional symbols and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonconventional symbol or abbreviation is disclosed as equivalent to a conventional symbol or to a specific sequence of conventional symbols, interpret the disclosure as though it were expressed using the equivalent conventional symbol(s) to determine inclusion requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonconventional ambiguity symbol is not equivalent to a conventional ambiguity symbol, interpret it as 'n' for nucleotides or 'X' for amino acids when determining whether paragraph 6 requires inclusion or paragraph 7 prohibits inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'specifically defined' (paragraph 3(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Specifically defined' means any nucleotide other than those represented by the symbol 'n' and any amino acid other than those represented by the symbol 'X' as listed in Annex I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counting specifically defined residues, treat conventional ambiguity symbols other than 'n' (nucleotides) and other than 'X' (amino acids) as specifically defined (e.g., IUPAC ambiguity codes K, V, R count as specifically defined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Most encompassing sequence rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a sequence is enumerated only once but described in multiple embodiments (variations), ST.26 requires inclusion of only the single enumerated sequence that has been enumerated by its residues — construed to be the most encompassing sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of further annotation, 'n' and 'X' are construed to represent any nucleotide or amino acid. The 'most encompassing' sequence uses ambiguity symbols that are most restrictive while including the most disclosed embodiments. Inclusion of additional specific sequences is strongly encouraged when they represent key embodiments and for more thorough searching and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper usage of ambiguity symbol 'n'
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbol 'n' may not be used to represent anything other than a single nucleotide; is construed as any one of 'a','c','g','t/u' except where used with further description; should be used (with further description) to represent modified nucleotides, 'unknown' nucleotides, abasic sites; may be used to represent sequence variants when 'n' is the most restrictive ambiguity symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'n' to represent non-nucleotide moieties (e.g., spacers). If disclosure uses 'n' to include non-nucleotides, consult ST.26 paragraph 15 to select an appropriate representation (e.g., split into segments, use 'v' for a/c/g when C3 spacer included, or annotate spacers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper usage of ambiguity symbol 'X'
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbol 'X' may not be used to represent anything other than a single amino acid; is construed as any one of the standard amino acids except where used with further description; should be used (with further description) to represent modified amino acids, 'unknown' amino acids; may be used to represent sequence variants when 'X' is the most restrictive ambiguity symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a conventional abbreviation (e.g., Xaa) is used nonconventionally, consult the disclosure to determine the specific amino acid(s) and represent using conventional single-letter codes (or 'X' if no conventional symbol available), with required feature annotations to explain modifications or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer conventional symbols for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence should be disclosed in a patent application by 'enumeration of its residues' using conventional symbols from Annex I (Tables for nucleotides and amino acids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conventional abbreviations or full names are used instead of symbols, or where conventional symbols are used nonconventionally, consult the disclosure explanation to confirm conventional usage; nonconventional usage may change whether ST.26 requires inclusion or prohibits inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonconventional ambiguity interpreted as 'n' or 'X'
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonconventional nucleotide ambiguity symbol is used and is not equivalent to a conventional ambiguity symbol in Annex I, interpret the residue as 'n' to determine inclusion per paragraph 6 vs paragraph 7. Similarly, nonconventional amino acid ambiguity symbols are interpreted as 'X'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation is only for deciding inclusion/representation in the listing; further description/feature annotation may be required to explain the nonconventional symbol's intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of D-amino acids (paragraph 28 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: D-amino acids should be represented in the sequence listing as the corresponding unmodified L-amino acid; any modified amino acid not covered in Annex I must be represented by 'X'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feature key 'SITE' plus qualifier 'NOTE' for each D-amino acid with the complete unabbreviated D-amino acid name. Also provide SITE/NOTE for modified residues (e.g., Nle). For circular peptides, applicant must choose residue position 1 and indicate circularity via feature key 'REGION' and NOTE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation for modified amino acids and chemical-structure enumerated residues
rubrics_metrics.description: When amino acids are enumerated by chemical structure or include modified residues, represent the sequence using conventional symbols where possible (use 'X' for modified residues that cannot be represented), and annotate the modified residues in the feature table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feature key 'SITE' with qualifier 'NOTE' that provides the complete unabbreviated name of the modified residue; annotate terminal modifications (acetylation, methylation) with SITE/NOTE; alternative representations may be provided but full annotation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of shorthand formulas and repeated units
rubrics_metrics.description: For shorthand formulas (e.g., (G4z)n) where unexpanded formula cannot be given a definite length, consider the unexpanded formula and represent the most encompassing enumerated peptide (e.g., GGGGX where z=any amino acid => X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate with REGION (e.g., '>5') and NOTE describing that the entire sequence can be repeated one or more times. Caution that this preferred representation is directed to provision on filing date; post-filing listings may be different to avoid adding subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segments separated by non-nucleotide spacers (C3 spacer example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an enumerated nucleotide sequence is interrupted by a non-nucleotide spacer (e.g., a C3 spacer), the spacer is not a nucleotide and the segments on either side are treated as separate nucleotide sequences if each contains >=10 specifically defined nucleotides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include each qualifying segment as a separate sequence in the listing with its own SEQ ID. Describe the nucleotide attached to the spacer in a feature table (feature key 'misc_feature' and qualifier 'note') indicating the presence of the spacer joined to another sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling 'n' that includes non-nucleotide alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If the disclosure defines 'n' as including nucleotides and a non-nucleotide (e.g., a C3 spacer), then 'n' cannot represent the spacer in the sequence listing; use the most restrictive conventional symbol for nucleotide alternatives (e.g., 'v' for a/c/g) and represent non-nucleotide spacer by splitting into separate segments and annotating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the most encompassing single sequence using restrictive ambiguity symbols for nucleotide options. Optionally include the two segments separated by spacer as separate sequences if essential. Annotate spacers with 'misc_feature' note naming the spacer (complete chemical name or common name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abasic site treated as nucleotide when part of a sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: An abasic site is considered a 'nucleotide' when it is part of a nucleotide sequence; where abasic interrupts specifically defined residues, the entire enumerated sequence including the abasic site may meet the threshold and must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent the abasic site in the sequence listing as 'n' and further describe it in a feature table using feature key 'modified_base' and mandatory qualifier 'mod_base' value 'OTHER', plus a 'note' describing the modified base as an abasic site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleic acid analogues (e.g., GNA) are sequences of nucleotides
rubrics_metrics.description: Residues comprising nucleic acid analogues are considered nucleotides per ST.26 paragraph 3(d)(i)(B); if enumeration yields >10 specifically defined residues they must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include representation in the direction that mimics 5'->3' (left-to-right that mimics 5'-end to 3'-end). Describe the modified nucleotides using feature key 'modified_base' with 'mod_base'='OTHER' and a 'note' with complete unabbreviated name. A single INSDFeature element can describe the entire sequence if location covers the range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting IUPAC ambiguity codes vs 'n' for 'specifically defined' residues
rubrics_metrics.description: IUPAC-IUB ambiguity codes (e.g., K, V, R, etc.) correspond to nucleotide symbols in Annex I and count as specifically defined nucleotides; only 'n' is the non-specific symbol excluded from 'specifically defined'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counting specifically defined nucleotides to apply paragraph 6 or 7, treat ambiguity codes other than 'n' as specifically defined. A sequence with fewer than ten specifically defined nucleotides must not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most-encompassing embodiment determines inclusion when symbol used both conventionally and nonconventionally
rubrics_metrics.description: When a symbol (e.g., 'N') is used in some embodiments as 'any nucleotide' and in others to denote specific nucleotides, only the most encompassing embodiment (e.g., 'any nucleotide') is considered when determining if the sequence must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the most encompassing embodiment results in fewer than the threshold of specifically defined residues, paragraph 6 does not require inclusion. However, including alternative sequences that represent key embodiments is highly recommended, with annotations (e.g., misc_difference replace qualifiers) if fewer alternatives are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonconventional use of 'n' as a specific nucleotide
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'n' is used in a disclosure in a nonconventional manner to represent only a specific nucleotide (e.g., 'n' is c), interpret the sequence as though the conventional symbol were used (i.e., treat 'n' as 'c') and count specifically defined residues accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent the sequence in the listing using the conventional symbol (e.g., 'c') and include it if it meets the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional abbreviation Xaa used nonconventionally for amino acids
rubrics_metrics.description: If conventional abbreviation Xaa (or similar) is used in a nonconventional manner with position-specific definitions, consult the explanation and represent each position using the conventional single-letter symbol(s) (e.g., J for Leu/Ile) with appropriate annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where positions are defined as specific amino acids in the disclosure, replace Xaa with the corresponding conventional symbol(s) and include feature table annotations elaborating alternative residues or variant meanings (e.g., VARIANT feature with NOTE qualifier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Branched nucleic acid sequences: include linear 3'-5' joined segments
rubrics_metrics.description: For branched nucleic acid sequences, the linear portions containing ten or more specifically defined nucleotides wherein adjacent nucleotides are joined 3' to 5' must be included in the sequence listing; portions linked by non-nucleotide moieties that do not contain ten such nucleotides must not be included as separate sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include qualifying branches as separate sequences and annotate them (e.g., first nucleotide described as modified using 'misc_feature' and 'note' stating this is one branch of a branched polynucleotide). Do not include horizontal/non-linear portions lacking 10 consecutive 3'->5' nucleotides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstandard residues such as pseudouridine handled as 'n'; RNA 'u' vs 't' convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstandard residues (e.g., pseudouridine 'Ψ') that are equivalent to an ambiguity for which only 'n' is the conventional symbol must be represented as 'n'. Additionally, in sequence listings 'u' cannot be used to represent uracil in RNA sequences; 't' will be construed as uracil in RNA (paragraph 14 guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace nonstandard symbols with the appropriate conventional ambiguity ('n') and represent sequences in the required nucleotide-letter conventions. Ensure mandatory qualifiers (e.g., 'mol_type' for 'source') are set appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on representing sequences with undefined internal gaps as a single sequence (paragraph 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.26 paragraph 37 prohibits inclusion of any sequence that contains an undefined gap (undefined number of 'n' or 'X' residues) as a single sequence. Portions adjacent to the gap that contain the threshold number of specifically defined residues must be included separately; portions below threshold must not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a portion adjacent to an undefined gap contains >=4 specifically defined amino acids (for peptides), represent that portion as a separate sequence and annotate with SITE/NOTE to indicate linkage to a larger sequence containing an undefined gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: CDS feature key and representation of coding sequences (paragraphs 88-90)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an encoding nucleotide sequence and its translated peptide, include the nucleotide sequence (if >10 specifically defined nucleotides) and the peptide sequence (if >4 specifically defined amino acids). Use the 'CDS' feature key and set INSDFeature_location to identify the entire coding region including the stop codon; include 'translation' qualifier with peptide sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonstandard genetic code applies, include 'transl_table' qualifier with the appropriate table number; include 'protein_id' qualifier specifying the sequence identification number of the translated peptide. Do not include stop codons in the peptide sequence in the sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignments and shorthand characters (dots and dashes) are interpreted as enumerated residues
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence alignments that use dots to indicate identity with the sequence above and dashes for absence of residues are treated as enumerated residues: dots count as specifically defined residues (same as the referenced residue) and dashes indicate absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert alignments to full enumerated sequences (replace dots with explicit residues) and count specifically defined residues for threshold determination. Include each species' sequence that meets the threshold as separate SEQ IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of single enumerated sequence with enumerated alternative residues (paragraph 91bis/92(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a single enumerated sequence includes alternative residues at positions, ST.26 requires inclusion of the single most-encompassing enumerated sequence; where ambiguity symbols are appropriate, use the most restrictive symbol that includes the disclosed alternatives (e.g., J for Leu/Ile, X for any amino acid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate variants with a VARIANT feature and NOTE qualifier to explain alternatives. Although only the single enumerated sequence is required, inclusion of additional specific sequences representing key embodiments is highly recommended and may be added as separate SEQ IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdependent multiple variations (paragraph 92(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a primary sequence contains multiple interdependent variable positions, include the enumerated primary sequence using the appropriate ambiguity symbols (use the most restrictive symbol permitted by paragraph 15) and strongly consider including explicit sequences for the major interdependent embodiments as separate entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 15 requires using the most restrictive symbol for variable positions; for interdependent variations, include the enumerated sequence and add the representative variants as separate sequences (examples provided). Annotate to explain which ambiguity codes (b, v, h, d, etc.) correspond to which sets of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution regarding filing-date vs post-filing sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance and preferred representations in this document are directed to provision of a sequence listing on the filing date of a patent application. The same representation may not be applicable to a sequence listing provided subsequent to the filing date because of potential added-subject-matter concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing sequence listings after the filing date, consider whether added or clarified information could be considered new subject matter by an IPO. Consult applicable IPO practice for post-filing sequence listings and consider including additional explanatory annotation or separate sequence entries as necessary.
